title: Seizures
description: Uncontrolled body movements or a sudden change in awareness caused by abnormal brain activity. May be due to epilepsy, fever, head injury, or other causes.

recognition_questions.q: Is the person having jerking movements they cannot control?
Is the seizure lasting more than 5 minutes, or is this their first seizure?
Are they injuring themselves or struggling to breathe?

immediate_safety_warnings: Do not restrain the person or put anything in their mouth.
Protect them from injury by moving hard objects away.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Stay calm. Time the seizure from when it starts.
Clear the area of hard or sharp objects. Protect the head with something soft.
Do not restrain them or put anything in their mouth.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Restraint causes injury; objects in the mouth block the airway.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Call 112 if the seizure lasts more than 5 minutes, if it is a first seizure, if injuries occur, or if the person is pregnant or a child/infant.
Once jerking stops, gently turn the person onto their side (recovery position) and tilt their head back.
Stay with them until fully awake and oriented. Reassure them.

actions_to_avoid: Do not put anything in their mouth (spoon, finger, cloth).
Do not give food or water until fully alert.
Do not move them unless they are in danger.

escalation_conditions.condition: Seizure in pregnancy, or with a serious injury

escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; suspect febrile convulsion; keep cool

approved_alternatives.alternative: Folded jacket, cloth, or a rolled item of clothing under the head

follow_up_requirements: Known epileptics should see their doctor if the pattern changes.

age_specific_pathways.child: Febrile seizures are common in children 6 months–5 years; cool the child, do not over-wrap; seek care if first episode or prolonged.
age_specific_pathways.infant: Any seizure in an infant needs urgent assessment.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
